text: An LLM's knowledge has a training cutoff and has never seen your specific workspace. Ask it which table has customer churn data, and it either admits it doesn't know, or guesses a plausible table name that doesn't exist.
Grounding means giving the model actual, current, relevant content at question time. RAG does that in four stages: embed, index, retrieve, and generate.

Without RAG, a question goes straight to the model's memory and might come back hallucinated. With RAG, the question first retrieves real content, and the answer is grounded in what was actually retrieved.

Embedding makes text comparable by meaning. Indexing makes retrieval fast at scale. Retrieval is the grounding step itself. Generation turns retrieved facts into a coherent answer, not where the facts come from.
This lesson stays conceptual on purpose — no embedding model chosen, no index built yet. Next up: chunking real catalog metadata and actually building a vector index over it.
